answer: To rename a web link (menu item) on your site: Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Choose Rename to change the name of the item on your site menu.

First, make sure you clicked Publish after changing the og:image. If the old image still appears when sharing, the platform may be showing cached data. For Facebook, use the Facebook Debugger (https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/), enter your URL, and click 'Scrape Again' (you may need to click it multiple times); Facebook can take time to process new information. For LinkedIn, use the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/), enter your URL, and note that it can take up to a week for the new image to appear in LinkedIn shares. Also verify your image has an aspect ratio of 1.91:1 (width 1.9x the height) to avoid cropping issues. If you didn't set a page-specific og:image, the site-wide og:image is used instead.

To see what items customers added to their cart, use the Wix Stores reports in your site's dashboard under the Stores section. The 'Most Abandoned Products' report shows products visitors placed in a cart but didn't buy, while the 'Abandoned Carts Funnel', 'Abandoned Carts Funnel Over Time', and 'Abandoned Carts Summary' reports show how many carts were abandoned and recovered. The 'Store Conversion Funnel' and 'Store Conversion Funnel Over Time' reports also track the 'added to cart' step in the purchasing process. To see how items were sold, use the 'Sales by Product Variant' report to see which variants (e.g., size, color) are selling most, the 'Sales by Product Category' report for sales broken down by category, or the general Sales reports (under the Sales section) such as 'Sales by item' and 'Item sales over time' for detailed breakdowns of specific items sold.

To identify low stock, you would monitor the inventory numbers in the Inventory tab or within the product settings, but there is no separate 'low stock' status or alert described in these docs.

To add delivery information to your product page, add an info section when creating or editing your product to provide additional information. Then, in your editor, go to the Product Page settings, click the Design tab, and under Info Sections select a layout (Collapse, Stack, Tabs, or Columns) to display this information on the page.

For a business account, if your Wix Payments status is 'Accepting Payments', you have connected the account but have not completed the account setup or verification process, so additional information is required before the account becomes 'Active' and you can receive payouts. According to the verification checklist for a business account, you must ensure: your first/middle/last name and date of birth match your photo ID; bank account number(s) are entered correctly; your company's name and registration number/tax ID match the company's registered information; your Doing Business As name matches what appears on customers' statements; you enter a physical address (PO Boxes not accepted) and upload an address verification document such as a utility bill issued within the last 6 months; the Legal Business Name, Shareholder and VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN match those associated with your business bank account; you upload a document proving the validity and ownership of the VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN during registration; you add a Business Description (select Business Type and describe products/services); and you upload a color copy of your photo ID and a bank statement. During the process Wix may request further information (e.g., government-issued photo ID and bank statement) to be uploaded to your Wix Payments Dashboard. Verification may take up to 7 business days, and you have 30 days from the first transaction to complete setup/verification or the account will be suspended.

The documentation does not provide specific dollar amounts for upgrading an email plan. For Email Marketing, the cost depends on the package you select based on the number of emails you plan to send per month and the additional features you need. For Google Workspace business email, the price depends on the plan tier you choose (Business Starter, Business Standard, or Business Plus) and is purchased separately from site Premium plans. To view exact pricing, go to Email Marketing in your site's dashboard, click Upgrade under Monthly Balance, and compare the available plans, or check the options when purchasing a Business Email in your Wix account.

In the Automation Builder, when editing your automated email template, you can add personalized content (also called dynamic values or variables) to insert the recipient's name. Go to Automations in your site's dashboard, create or edit an automation with 'Send an email' as the action, click the action to open the panel, then under 'Create an email' select 'Edit' and add personalized content to the email. These dynamic values display different information to each user based on their data, such as their name. If you select Wix Forms as your trigger, make sure to choose the specific form that the personalized content should be pulled from so the correct options are displayed. Note that personalized content does not appear in test emails, but recipients will see it when the automation is sent.

Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor. If your site is not displaying correctly on mobile, you can optimize the layout using the Page Layout Optimizer: click Page Layout Optimizer on the left side of the mobile Editor, then click Optimize Now. You can also manually adjust the layout by dragging elements to different locations in the mobile Editor. Note: If you are using the latest Editor experience, you won't have access to the Page Layout Optimizer tool because Wix automatically optimizes your mobile layout in the new Editor experience. Changes made to the mobile layout do not affect your desktop site.

This behavior matches the strip background scaling settings described in the documentation. When an image is set as a strip or column background, selecting 'Original Size' causes parts of the image to be cut off, while selecting 'Tile' displays the image in tile formation (multiplied) across the available space. To resolve this, go to your editor, select the image on the strip, click 'Change Strip Background' (or 'Change Column Background' if it's in a column), click Settings, scroll to Scaling & Positioning, and change 'How's the image scaled?' to 'Scale to Fill'. Then select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to focus on the desired part of the image. Alternatively, you can crop the image to better fit the available space.

According to the documentation, Wix Stores is designed for selling physical and digital products (including dropshipping items and product subscriptions). For selling services, Wix offers separate solutions—such as the ability to provide services and take bookings—which are distinct from the Wix Stores online store features.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve this error: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact Wix support and they will be happy to help.

The provided documentation does not contain information about setting up an automation triggered by a client's birthday. While the documentation explains how to configure a 'Send an email' action and how to create a class with a 'Free' pricing option, it does not describe a birthday trigger or how to set up an automation based on a contact's date of birth.

To update inventory for many product variants at once, use the bulk edit feature for product variants. Go to Store Products in your site's dashboard, select a product with product options, and make sure the 'Manage pricing and inventory for variants' toggle is enabled. Click Edit, then select which variants to update (all variants, variants with specific options, or specific variants via checkboxes). Choose 'Edit Inventory' from the options at the top right, enter the inventory amount, and click Apply. For advanced bulk edits across multiple products, go to the Inventory tab. Note that you can manage a total of 1000 variants, so 100 products with 3 options each (300 variants) is within the supported limit.

Site visitors can check your calendar by viewing the calendar app you've added to your website. Once you add a calendar (such as the Google Event Calendar) and configure the visibility settings to show specific events to site visitors, they can see your schedule, availability, and upcoming events directly on your site. You control what visitors see by selecting which calendars are visible and whether events appear with full details, as busy, or as private.

For unwanted gaps at the bottom of your desktop page (between page content and footer, or below the footer on the live site), you can try the following solutions from the Wix Editor: 1) Adjust the page height by clicking and dragging the Adjust Page Height icon to remove space between content and the footer. Note: If your page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to access the main part of the page. 2) If the gap appears below the footer on your live site because your content is shorter than the page length, you can: change the page background color to match the footer color, add more content to the page, resize the footer to make it longer, or check the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap. 3) If gaps appear between full-width elements (like lines, menus, or galleries) and other elements, use the Zoom out to 50% function to move elements and delete spaces, or manually drag elements to remove gaps.

If you previously verified your site with Google manually (using the meta tag method in Google Search Console), your site is already connected to Google. You don't need to complete the 'Connect site to Google' step in your SEO Setup Checklist. If that step is still marked as not completed, you can ignore it.

To add and format text in a Rich Text field in the CMS: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click the relevant collection, then click the Rich Text field for the specific item. Enter your text and use the formatting options at the top of the editor (e.g., Bold, Themes, Alignment, Link). Click the Expand icon to edit in a larger window if needed. Repeat for each collection item. The Rich Text editor uses your site's font theme, so formatting will match your site's heading and paragraph styles.

If your dynamic list page is not displaying items alphabetically despite having sort conditions set in the dataset settings, check the following based on the documentation: 1) Verify the dataset mode is set to "Read" or "Read & Write" — datasets in "Write" mode cannot read collection content and therefore cannot apply sort conditions. 2) Confirm that any "Mirror on Site" feature enabled in your collection view is not overriding your dataset sort — dataset sorts always override the order set in a mirrored collection view. 3) If you are sorting a Text field that contains both letters and numbers, note that the system applies alphabetic sorting (e.g., P101, P120, P1200, P123) rather than numerical order; to sort numerically, use a Number field type without letters.

If your subscription is in a grace period and recurring retries are enabled, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from your existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. You can also manually retry the payment by going to the My Subscriptions page in the Members Area, clicking Submit Payment next to the failed subscription, and choosing your existing payment method. Alternatively, the site owner can manually submit the payment using your card details with your permission by going to Subscriptions in their dashboard, selecting the subscription, clicking Collect Payment, then Submit payment, and entering your card details.

To resize the image: Click the image in your Editor, then drag the handles on the edges of the image to the size you want (corner handles keep the original proportions). To add text to your new section: Click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click a category (e.g., Text), and drag the element onto the section. If you want to place text on top of the image itself, add a transparent container box: Click Add Elements, select Box, drag it onto the image, then make it transparent via Change Design > Customize Design > Fill Color & Opacity (set Background slider to 0%), and drag your text elements onto the box.

However, the retrieved context does not provide specific troubleshooting steps for resolving a glitch where menu item text fails to update.

To create a duplicate of your site from the dashboard for testing: Go to your site's dashboard, click Home on the left, click the Site Actions icon, then click Duplicate Site. Enter a name for the duplicate site and click Duplicate. Any changes you make to the copy will not affect your live site. Note that the duplicate does not include store orders, invoices, contacts, members, email campaigns, third-party app settings, Google Operations logs, or Velo secrets.

For the Wix Video player: Go to your editor, click the Wix Video player on your page, click Settings, click the Player tab, and click the 'Autoplay on load' toggle to enable or disable automatic playback. Note: Videos set to autoplay always start on mute due to browser restrictions. The Autoplay on load toggle is not available for the strip and slider layouts. For the Single Video Player (e.g., Twitch videos), the toggle is labeled 'Autoplays' in the playback options when adding the video. For Wix Blog videos in the feed or post list, go to Settings > Design tab > Video Settings and select 'Autoplay' from the drop-down menu.

To resolve the company verification error, re-enter your company registration number (or business number/EIN/UTR/tax ID) ensuring that your company's name and its registration number/tax ID exactly match the company's registered information. Then upload a company registration document that proves the validity and ownership of the VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN during registration. Also confirm that the Legal Business Name and the VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN entered in the form matches those associated with your business bank account.

To access the Google Maps element in your footer, open the Layers panel by clicking the Layers icon at the bottom of your editor, click Footer, then find and click the Google Maps element in the list to select it. If the map is behind another element, use the Overlapping Items feature: right-click the element covering the map, hover over Overlapping Items, and select the Google Maps element. If you still cannot select it, check whether your footer is frozen: click the footer, click the Settings icon, and disable the Freeze Footer toggle. Once selected using either method, you can remove the element.

To require customers to sign up before making purchases, restrict access to the Cart Page so only signed-in members can access it. First, add the Wix Members Area to your site if you don't already have it. Then, in your editor, go to Pages & Menu (Wix Editor) or Pages (Studio Editor) and navigate to your Cart Page: for Wix Stores only, click Store Pages > Cart Page; for Wix Bookings only, click Bookings Pages > Cart Page; for Wix Restaurants Orders (New) or 2 business solutions, click Cart & Thank You > Cart Page. Click the Settings icon next to Cart Page (or More Actions > Settings in Studio Editor), select the Permissions tab, and click Members Only. You can then choose to allow All members, or limit access to Only selected members or paying customers (such as a specific member role or clients who purchased a pricing plan). Note: Customers may still complete orders without signing in through certain methods that bypass the Cart Page, such as the Buy Now button on Product Pages.

Since you have a Google Workspace admin account, you can reset the password for your second business Gmail account as an admin. Sign in to your Google Admin account, click Password, then Reset Password. Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a new password yourself. Optionally, enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle to require the user to change it. Click Reset. You can then click 'Click to copy password' to copy it, or choose to email the password to the user, then click Done. Note: By default, the password minimum length is 8 characters.

Payouts are placed on hold when there is a failed payout or an unresolved verification issue blocking the transfer to your bank account. The held amount includes the failed payout plus any other available funds that cannot be sent due to the issue. To identify and resolve the problem, click on the specific payout in your Wix Payments dashboard to see the reason for the failure and the instructions provided. Common causes include incorrect bank account details (the bank account holder's name must match the Wix Payments account owner name) or the bank account not being able to receive EFT/ACH transfers. You can verify and correct your bank details by going to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, clicking Manage next to Wix Payments, then clicking Edit Account Details next to Account Details, checking the information under Bank Details, correcting it if necessary, and clicking Resubmit. Once the issue is resolved, the funds will be included in your next scheduled payout.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with your Wix site, first create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant. Then, copy your GA4 measurement ID from the Web stream details in Google Analytics. In your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, click the Show More icon in the top right corner, and click Edit. Paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up (ensure there are no extra spaces before the code), optionally select the IP Anonymization checkbox if you want to hide visitor IP addresses, and click Save. If you are upgrading from Universal Analytics, note that UA properties stopped collecting data on July 1, 2023, and you can use both properties simultaneously by connecting your UA tracking ID to your GA4 property in the Google Analytics Admin section under Manage connected site tags.

According to the Google Ads with Wix refund policy, ad credits added to Google Ads with Wix are paid with a monthly subscription or a one-time payment, and these payments are non-refundable. Therefore, you cannot request a refund for your Google Ads campaign. If you pause a campaign, your remaining ad credits remain in your account and can be used to resume the campaign at any time, but the payments already made are not refundable.

Yes. The free domain voucher is not applied at the plan checkout. You receive the 1-year free domain voucher with the initial purchase of a selected yearly or multi-year Premium plan. After you purchase the plan, the voucher appears in the Premium Vouchers page in your Wix account, where you can view and claim it. You then use the voucher separately when purchasing a new domain (go to Domains > Buy a Domain), and it must be redeemed within 2 months of purchasing your plan. If you purchased a monthly plan instead of yearly, or purchased a domain before purchasing the plan, you would not be eligible for the voucher.

Since your site is published and not password protected, try these steps from the Wix documentation to get your site indexed by Google:

1. **Check that search engines can index your site**: Go to your SEO Dashboard, select 'Go to SEO Settings' under Tools and settings, and make sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled.

2. **Check that search engines can index the specific page**: In your site's Editor, check the page's SEO settings to ensure you haven't selected the option to prevent search engines from indexing that page.

3. **Check for a 'noindex' robots meta tag**: Verify your page doesn't have a 'noindex' tag in its HTML code, which tells search engines not to index it.

4. **Check for 301 redirects**: Go to your SEO Dashboard, select 'Go to URL Redirect Manager' under Tools and settings. If your page has a 301 redirect, hover over it and click the Delete icon.

5. **Reset your page's canonical tag**: In your page's SEO settings, go to the Advanced SEO tab, click Additional Tags, click the More Actions icon on 'canonical', select Edit, then click 'Reset to Default' and Apply.

6. **Ensure the page has enough content**: Pages with little content may return errors or be removed from Google's index. Include at least 250-400 words on the page.

7. **Add internal links**: Add links from other pages on your site to the page you want indexed, as search engines use these to discover and understand your pages.

8. **Use the Wix SEO Setup Checklist**: Complete the checklist in your SEO Dashboard, which helps optimize your site and submits it directly to Google for indexing.

9. **Submit your sitemap or individual URLs**: You can submit your sitemap directly to Google, or submit individual page URLs for more accuracy after making changes.

10. **Check index status and request indexing**: Use Google's URL Inspection tool or the Wix Site Inspection tool to check if your page is indexed and diagnose issues. If needed, click 'Request Indexing' in the URL Inspection tool.

11. **Check for manual actions**: Use Google Search Console to check if Google has applied any manual actions to your page that prevent it from appearing in search results.

Note: It can take some time for Google to crawl and index your site after these changes. Search engines cannot guarantee that every page will be indexed, and this is normal in many cases.

To change the order of items in your CMS collection and have it reflect on your live site, follow these steps from the documentation: 1) Go to CMS in your site's dashboard (or click CMS in your editor, then Your Collections). 2) Click the relevant collection and select the view at the top you want to use. 3) Choose how to sort: either add a sort condition (click Sort > + Add a Sort > select the field and order > Add Sort) or manually reorder items (ensure Table is selected as the layout type, click the Reorder icon next to an item, and drag it up or down). 4) Click Mirror on Site at the top of the collection and enable the toggle next to 'Mirror item order on the site'. Important notes: Any sorts you've added to datasets will override the order set in your mirrored collection view. Also, you cannot enable 'Mirror on Site' with external collections and Wix Blocks collections. If you delete a collection view that has mirroring enabled, the order on the site reverts back to the order in which items were created.

For a page without a footer, click on the page itself and drag the Adjust Page Height handle located at the bottom of the page to the desired position. To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) and eliminate the 4GB native memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. This disables compressed references, allowing native memory to grow beyond the 4GB mark. However, this will result in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so the Java heap size should be adjusted to a larger value and garbage collection should be monitored and retuned as required. Note that before using this as a solution, you should first rule out the possibility of a native memory leak, since disabling compressed references allows native memory to grow unbounded.

The issue may occur when the underlying network connection becomes invalid after a period of inactivity. A typical cause is a firewall between the Application Server and the Database that has a policy to discard network connections that remain idle for some time. To resolve this, configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool by setting the Minimum connections to 0 (to avoid keeping connections in the pool that may have been idle longer than the Unused timeout) and setting the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that their sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout.

The syndication fails because the Administrator user (Domain Admin) retrieved via com.presence.connect.wmmcomms.UserManagementServiceImpl.getPortalAdministrator() exists on the Base Portal but not on the Realm configured to the Virtual Portal, or does not have access to the Virtual Portal. This can also manifest as a MemberNotFoundException (e.g., EJPSG0002E: Requested Member does not exist) for the admin user. To resolve this, the Admin user must be made visible on both the base and virtual Portals, and when syndicating to Virtual Portals, the Administrator User listed as the Domain Admin must have access to the Virtual Portal.

General guidance for diagnosing java.lang.StackOverflowError indicates examining javacores, thread dumps, or system dumps for recursive method calls (repeated stack frames), as the stack may contain thousands of recursively called entries (e.g., 1000 entries). If the recursion is legitimate, increasing the thread stack size may allow for larger thread stacks; however, if the overflow continues, the specific code causing the recursion must be identified from the thread dumps.

The error indicates a SQL Server query processor resource issue with the Case Analyzer store. To resolve this, set the analyzer.db.updateMode parameter to BATCH in the Case Analyzer store database. Run the following query in the Case Analyzer store database: UPDATE X_CAProperties SET PropValue='BATCH' WHERE PropName ='analyzer.db.updateMode'. IBM support recommends this setting to circumvent various performance-related symptoms, and Microsoft JDBC drivers work better and are more stable with the BATCH setting compared to the default CUSTOM_BATCH.

For IBM BPM 8.5 (which is based on WebSphere Application Server v8 and later), use the WASServiceHelper.bat utility located in the bin directory of the installation to create a Windows service for the Deployment Manager profile, rather than using BPMConfig. This utility acts as a front end for WASService.exe and creates a Windows service entry using parameters such as: -add "ServiceName" -serverName "dmgr" -profilePath "C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\profiles\Dmgr01" -logRoot "C:\...\logs\dmgr" -logFile "C:\...\WS_startdmgr.log" -encodeParams -stopArgs "-username ... -password ..." -startType manual -restart false. Once created, the dmgr can be started and managed as a Windows service independent of the logged-in user session.

When the base entry and the name in the repository are different, and the clearCache functionality is used with clearEntity mode, the virtual member manager (VMM) still looks in the cache and retrieves the entity from the cache instead of fetching it from the LDAP server. The exception java.lang.IllegalStateException: SRVE0199E: OutputStream already obtained is caused by attempting to associate two output streams with one JSP file. In JSP, the default output stream is always created when the JSP has been translated to a servlet; creating and associating another output stream (for example, by calling getOutputStream() when the output stream has already been obtained) results in this error.

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs), Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks are stored with 32-bit pointers and must be allocated in the first 4GB of address space (the low-memory region). Even when the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust this low-memory region under 4GB. If the Java heap is also small (-Xmx) and allocated in the lower 4GB, it competes for this limited space. When these native artifacts cannot fit in the lower 4GB, the JVM throws a Native OutOfMemory (NOOM). To resolve this, use -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> to place the heap above 4GB, or set -Xmx4G. Starting in Java 6.0.16.3, Java 6.1.8.3, Java 7.0.8.10, and Java 7.1.2.10, you can also use -Xmcrs to increase the amount of low memory the JVM reserves on startup. If the NOOM appears as 'Failed to create a thread' in javacores, the cause may instead be insufficient ulimit settings (nproc/-u on Linux, ulimit -r on AIX) restricting the number of threads per user.

No, JazzSM does not support HTTP access. By default, the Jazz for Service Management application server requires HTTPS access. While you can technically set up the environment for both HTTP and HTTPS, HTTP access is explicitly not supported for security reasons. The documentation states: 'For security reasons, HTTP access is disabled by default and is not supported.' Users must use the HTTPS secure port (default https://<host_name>:16311/ibm/console) for logging in to the Dashboard Application Services Hub.

The EIF probe is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after receiving the event (as shown in iptrace), causing the event to be dropped before it appears in EIF logs or reaches OMNIbus. To resolve this, change the ConnectionMode in the om_tec.config file on the ITM Server (TEMS) from 'ConnectionMode=co' (connection oriented) to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

The information is available in IBM Security Bulletin swg21968399 titled 'IBM Security Bulletin: IBM WebSphere MQ MQXR insecure passwords (CVE-2015-2012)'. The bulletin states that the Telemetry (MQXR) service can be configured to use SSL/TLS connections, but the passphrase used to access the keystore is written to the file system in clear text in a world-readable properties file. It affects IBM WebSphere MQ 8.0 (8.0.0.3 and earlier), 7.5 (7.5.0.5 and earlier), and 7.1 (7.1.0.6 and earlier). The CVSS Base Score is 2.1. Remediation requires installing fixpack 8.0.0.4 for MQ 8.0, applying interim fix IT09866 for MQ 7.5, or installing fixpack 7.1.0.7 for MQ 7.1.

Yes, you can disable RC4 ciphers in Tivoli Integrated Portal (TIP) by following these steps in WebSphere Application Server:

1. Log into the WebSphere Application Server and navigate to: SSL certificate and key management > SSL configurations > NodeDefaultSSLSettings > Quality of protection (QoP).
2. Select the RC4 ciphers from the "Selected ciphers" list, and then click the "<<Remove" button.
3. Click the "Apply" button, and then the "Save (to the master configuration)" link.
4. Restart TIP.
